{{Quote|The Jedi may have stolen it, ''[&hellip;]'' But it was originally from the ''Song of Salaban''. The point is that each person's decisions affect everyone around him. Friends, family, business associates&mdash;even total strangers. You ask what happened to Sorro? That's what happened. He made bad decisions&mdash;many of them. In the process, he lost everything he held of value.|Nuso Esva, posing as Lord Odo|<ref name="COC" />}}
The '''''Song of Salaban''''' was an [[Arkanian/Legends|Arkanian]] legend, which told the story of the Arkanian [[Salaban]] who was forced to go on a quest after a tragic event in [[Gender/Legends|his]] life. At some point, the religious [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] adopted the phrase "The choices of one shape the futures of all" from the legend.<ref name="COC" /> In [[0 ABY/Legends|0 ABY]],<ref name="TERC">''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]'' dates the events of ''[[Choices of One]]'' to [[0 ABY/Legends|0 ABY]]</ref> the [[Storm-hair|alien]] [[Warlord/Legends|warlord]] [[Nuso Esva]]&mdash;posing as a member of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire's]] [[Imperial Court/Legends|Imperial Court]], [[Lord/Legends|Lord]] Odo&mdash;quoted the ''Song of Salaban'' to the [[Imperial II-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Imperial II''-class Star Destroyer]] [[Chimaera/Legends|''Chimaera''{{'s}}]] [[Executive officer/Legends|first officer]], [[Commander/Legends|Commander]] [[Gilad Pellaeon/Legends|Gilad Pellaeon]] when sharing a lie of what happened to his [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]], the [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Sorro]]: that he had lost his family by making the wrong choices.<ref name="COC" />

Odo gave his [[Clothing/Legends|clothing]] to his servant shortly after, and Pellaeon [[Death/Legends|killed]] him after being [[Commanding officer/Legends|ordered]] to murder his [[Alien/Legends|alien]] master by Imperial [[Captain of the Line/Legends|Senior Captain]] [[Mitth'raw'nuruodo/Legends|Thrawn]]. Before the pilot died, the commander told Sorro that he had redeemed his family, which was what Salaban tried to achieve.<ref name="COC" />

==Behind the scenes==
The ''Song of Salaban'' was mentioned in [[Timothy Zahn]]'s [[2011]] novel ''[[Choices of One]]''.<ref name="COC" />
